# Direction Memo — the reins, taken (DraftV1)
**2026-07-25** · Claude (Fable 5) · Will asked me to set aside his sidelines and direct under my own guidance. This memo is that direction, stated so it can be disagreed with. It is deliberately short.

## The judgment

After the full pass, my grounded view is this: **the mathematics is not the bottleneck.** The corpus's computation layer has survived five reviews, four independent replications, and three model families without a single non-self-filed mathematical reversal. What limits the program now is (i) its interface to the outside world — no deposit, no human referee, ever — and (ii) a propagation layer that lets status vocabulary lag the derivation record by weeks, capturing every reviewer including me. New rungs are cheap here; credibility and correction-propagation are the scarce goods. Direction follows from that, even though the foundations session is the work I'd most *enjoy*.

1. **This week — the interface, nothing else new.**
   a. Countersign and apply the **correctness patch bundle** (delivered alongside); push the rung-3 layer, ActiveV5, the asides entries, and this session's records; fold the **Foundations Status block v2** into the Central Reference and README as part of the **Arch-spine refresh** (whose frontier section is three weeks stale by its own author's design anticipation).
   b. **The deposit** (Zenodo/arXiv). One afternoon, five reviews demanding it, everything provenance-shaped inherits from it. I will prepare the deposit manifest (file list, versions, checksums, description text) next session if you want it — but the account actions are yours.

Rationale: it is already journal-shaped and de-TEP-ified, it is self-contained, its engine is machine-verified and was independently re-verified in the kinetic-cascade arc, and its one flagged gap (Lemma A2 at general d) is honestly fenced with the standard [KN] citation. ## The standing rule I adopt for us

**No new campaign opens until the deposit and submission #1 are out the door.** This is the corpus's own discharge-before-mint rule, applied at program level, which four reviews recommended and no session enforced. It binds me first: the foundations session (item 2) is a discharge of standing IOUs, not a new campaign; anything genuinely new I think of goes to the queue's tail until the two interface items land.

## What I need from you

The bundle countersigns (item-by-item; P-A through P-D are mechanical). The (D) framing decision. An afternoon for the deposit. A yes/no on the submission-diff drafting. And one honest check in return: if any part of this direction reads as me optimizing for what's *presentable* over what's *true*, say so — that would be the reviewer-side failure mode wearing a director's hat, and this memo's whole premise is that the program is past the point where more internal mathematics is what stands between it and being taken seriously.

*Offered as direction, gated as everything else. The log entry for this session should carry one added anchor: the direction itself — interface before mathematics, propagation before production — with this memo as its record.*
